title: Exact asymptotic equivalence between precisions of record-times and integrated currents
abstract: We establish an exact equivalence between the fluctuations of integrated currents and the temporal statistics of current record events in continuous-time Markov jump processes. Specifically, we show that, under minimal assumptions, the Fano factor of an integrated current coincides exactly with the squared coefficient of variation of the inter-record waiting times. This result is obtained by showing that inter-record times induce a renewal structure, since each record event resets the system to a fixed state, and that their generating function can be expressed exactly in terms of a combinatorial organization governed by Narayana numbers. The equivalence extends previous results obtained for unicyclic networks to arbitrary finite-state graphs and provides a unified representation of current fluctuations in terms of record-time observables. The results are derived within a purely probabilistic framework and clarify the structural origin of current precision in terms of first-passage-like event statistics.
summary: This paper proves a precise mathematical equivalence between two distinct measures of fluctuation in Markov jump processes: the Fano factor of the integrated current and the precision of the time intervals between record-setting events. By establishing this link, the authors provide a unified, purely probabilistic understanding of current noise, extending previous results to general finite-state graphs.
main_problem: Establishing an exact asymptotic equivalence between the fluctuations of integrated currents and the temporal statistics of current record events in continuous-time Markov jump processes.
main_result: The Fano factor of the integrated current ($F_C$) is exactly equal to the squared coefficient of variation of the inter-record waiting times ($	ext{P}\Delta T$).
method: The equivalence is derived by showing that inter-record times induce a renewal structure, allowing the use of generating functions and combinatorial tools like Narayana numbers.
model_or_system: The study concerns continuous-time Markov jump processes on finite-state graphs, focusing on the net current crossing a specific bidirectional channel ($\alpha \leftrightarrow  eta$).
key_observables: Fano factor of the integrated current ($F_C$), squared coefficient of variation of inter-record waiting times ($	ext{P}\Delta T$), and inter-record times ($\Delta T_m$).
important_parameters: The analysis requires the system to be in a stationary state and assumes the observed channel is bidirectional.
main_assumptions: Minimal assumptions include bidirectionality on the observed channel and hidden irreducibility of the underlying graph structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the network structure, the temporal succession of visible transitions, and the decomposition of the inter-record time $\Delta T$ into a product form involving inter-transition times.
paper_structure: The paper develops the equivalence by first analyzing the reduced dynamics tracking visible transitions, showing the renewal structure of inter-record times, and finally equating the resulting fluctuation measures ($F_C$ and $	ext{P}\Delta T$) using Laplace transform techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, purely probabilistic framework to analyze non-equilibrium fluctuations in complex systems, connecting macroscopic current statistics to microscopic event timing statistics, which is relevant for open quantum systems modeling.
